title: Systematic evaluation of Lianhua Qingwen against respiratory syncytial virus: Multi-mechanism insights and identification of an active ingredient U17.
authors: Li, Zhu; Liu, Bin; Xie, Yuqi; Cui, Zhanyu; Ye, Yi; Wei, Xiaotong; Wang, Yutao; Yang, Zifeng; Ma, Qinhai
one_liner_zh: 该研究评估连花清瘟抗呼吸道合胞病毒作用，涉及分子对接与病毒蛋白互作，但对象为病毒蛋白而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Lianhua Qingwen (LHQW), as a classic compound formulation of traditional Chinese medicine, holds significant value in antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory activities. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the anti-respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity of LHQW, elucidated its mechanisms of action, and identified its key active ingredients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The antiviral effects were assessed using in vitro cell models and in vivo models of young and immunosuppressed mice. Network pharmacology was employed to screen potential active ingredients of LHQW. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) were used to analyze the interaction between active ingredients and viral proteins. Changes in m(6)A modification and the expression of related enzymes were examined to explore epigenetic regulatory mechanisms. RESULTS: LHQW inhibited RSV replication in a dose-dependent manner, down-regulated the expression of inflammatory factors, and alleviated pulmonary pathological damage. These observations appeared to be associated with the potential suppression of the IKK-alpha/beta-NF-kappaB pathway and the modulation of m(6)A modification homeostasis. Using network pharmacology, the component U17 was identified, and it appeared to exhibit significant anti-RSV activity both in vitro and in vivo. U17 was shown to interact with the RSV-F protein during early infection, which may contribute to blocking viral entry. CONCLUSIONS: LHQW may exert its anti-RSV effects partly through mechanisms associated with the suppression of the IKK-alpha/beta-NF-kappaB pathway and the modulation of m(6)A epigenetic homeostasis. Notably, the constituent U17 emerges as a key active ingredient, which directly targets the RSV-F protein to block viral entry. These findings position U17 as a promising lead candidate for anti-RSV drug development and underscore the multi-target potential of traditional Chinese medicine in treating viral infections.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：连花清瘟（LHQW）作为传统中药的经典复方制剂，在抗病毒、抗炎和免疫调节活性方面具有重要价值。研究目的：本研究旨在系统评估LHQW的抗呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）活性，阐明其作用机制，并鉴定其关键活性成分。材料与方法：采用体外细胞模型及幼年和免疫抑制小鼠的体内模型评估抗病毒效果。通过网络药理学筛选LHQW的潜在活性成分。利用分子对接和表面等离子体共振（SPR）分析活性成分与病毒蛋白之间的相互作用。检测m(6)A修饰的变化及相关酶的表达，以探讨表观遗传调控机制。结果：LHQW以剂量依赖性方式抑制RSV复制，下调炎症因子的表达，并减轻肺部病理损伤。这些观察结果似乎与对IKK-alpha/beta-NF-kappaB通路的潜在抑制及m(6)A修饰稳态的调节相关。通过网络药理学，鉴定出成分U17，并显示其在体外和体内均表现出显著的抗RSV活性。U17被证明在早期感染阶段与RSV-F蛋白相互作用，这可能有助于阻断病毒进入。结论：LHQW可能部分通过抑制IKK-alpha/beta-NF-kappaB通路和调节m(6)A表观遗传稳态的机制发挥其抗RSV作用。值得注意的是，成分U17作为关键活性成分出现，直接靶向RSV-F蛋白以阻断病毒进入。这些发现将U17定位为抗RSV药物开发的有前景的先导候选物，并强调了中药在治疗病毒感染中的多靶点潜力。
